cur:manuscripts-rossano-christ-barabbas.summary: In an apse-like semicircle, Pilate sits enthroned behind a table flanked by imperial standards, surrounded by the crowd who cry out. In the lower register Christ stands calm and haloed among guards, while on the right the bound Barabbas is held by his captors. The page shows the decisive moment of the trial, when the people choose Barabbas over Christ.
facts: Unusually, the Rossano artist did not show the familiar hand-washing of Pilate but the opening of the trial and the choice between Christ and Barabbas, as discussed in the Wikipedia account of the manuscript.
Pilate's commanding position, with Christ lower and to one side, distinguishes these two trial pages from most later versions of the scene.
